From d97708701434ce72968e771976aaf9d3438fcafd Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Matt Evans <mattev@meta.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 11:17:52 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] vfio/pci: Clean up DMABUFs before disabling function

On device shutdown, make vfio_pci_core_close_device() call
vfio_pci_dma_buf_cleanup() before the function is disabled via
vfio_pci_core_disable().  This ensures that all access via DMABUFs is
revoked before the function's BARs become inaccessible.

This fixes an issue where, if the function is disabled first, a tiny
window exists in which the function's MSE is cleared and yet BARs
could still be accessed via the DMABUF.  The resources would also be
freed and up for grabs by a different driver.

Fixes: 5d74781ebc86c ("vfio/pci: Add dma-buf export support for MMIO regions")
Signed-off-by: Matt Evans <mattev@meta.com>
Reviewed-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>
Reviewed-by: Kevin Tian <kevin.tian@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Leon Romanovsky <leonro@nvidia.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20260415181752.1027604-1-mattev@meta.com
Signed-off-by: Alex Williamson <alex@shazbot.org>

diff --git a/drivers/vfio/pci/vfio_pci_core.c b/drivers/vfio/pci/vfio_pci_core.c
index ad52abc46c04..3f8d093aacf8 100644
--- a/drivers/vfio/pci/vfio_pci_core.c
+++ b/drivers/vfio/pci/vfio_pci_core.c
@@ -734,10 +734,10 @@ void vfio_pci_core_close_device(struct vfio_device *core_vdev)
 #if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_EEH)
 	eeh_dev_release(vdev->pdev);
 #endif
-	vfio_pci_core_disable(vdev);
-
 	vfio_pci_dma_buf_cleanup(vdev);
 
+	vfio_pci_core_disable(vdev);
+
 	mutex_lock(&vdev->igate);
 	vfio_pci_eventfd_replace_locked(vdev, &vdev->err_trigger, NULL);
 	vfio_pci_eventfd_replace_locked(vdev, &vdev->req_trigger, NULL);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file, `drivers/vfio/pci/vfio_pci_core.c`, to reorder two function calls in `vfio_pci_core_close_device()`. Specifically, `vfio_pci_dma_buf_cleanup(vdev)` is moved before `vfio_pci_core_disable(vdev)`.

**Modifications in each file:**
- **`drivers/vfio/pci/vfio_pci_core.c`**: Swapped the order of the cleanup and disable operations. Previously, the function was disabled first, then DMABUFs were cleaned up. Now, DMABUFs are cleaned up before disabling the function.

**Relationships between modifications:**
- The change ensures that all access via exported DMABUFs is revoked **before** the PCI function is disabled. This prevents a race condition where the function's memory space enable (MSE) could be cleared and BAR resources freed while still being accessible through a DMABUF. By cleaning up DMABUFs first, the patch guarantees that no stale references to BAR resources remain after the function is shut down.

Here is the commit message:
vfio/pci: Clean up DMABUFs before disabling function

On device shutdown, make vfio_pci_core_close_device() call
vfio_pci_dma_buf_cleanup() before the function is disabled via
vfio_pci_core_disable().  This ensures that all access via DMABUFs is
revoked before the function's BARs become inaccessible.

This fixes an issue where, if the function is disabled first, a tiny
window exists in which the function's MSE is cleared and yet BARs
could still be accessed via the DMABUF.  The resources would also be
freed and up for grabs by a different driver.

Fixes: 5d74781ebc86c ("vfio/pci: Add dma-buf export support for MMIO regions")
Signed-off-by: Matt Evans <mattev@meta.com>
Reviewed-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>
Reviewed-by: Kevin Tian <kevin.tian@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Leon Romanovsky <leonro@nvidia.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20260415181752.1027604-1-mattev@meta.com
Signed-off-by: Alex Williamson <alex@shazbot.org>

Here is the root cause:
The close_device function disabled the PCI function (vfio_pci_core_disable) before cleaning up DMABUFs (vfio_pci_dma_buf_cleanup). This allowed DMABUFs to still access BARs after MSE was cleared and resources were freed, potentially leading to use-after-free or access to reassigned resources.

Here is the patch:
 
 void vfio_pci_core_close_device(struct vfio_device *core_vdev)
 {
 	struct vfio_pci_core_device *vdev =
 		container_of(core_vdev, struct vfio_pci_core_device, vdev);
 
 	if (vdev->sriov_pf_core_dev) {
 		mutex_lock(&vdev->sriov_pf_core_dev->vf_token->lock);
 		WARN_ON(!vdev->sriov_pf_core_dev->vf_token->users);
 		vdev->sriov_pf_core_dev->vf_token->users--;
 		mutex_unlock(&vdev->sriov_pf_core_dev->vf_token->lock);
 	}
 #if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_EEH)
 	eeh_dev_release(vdev->pdev);
 #endif
-	vfio_pci_core_disable(vdev);
-
 	vfio_pci_dma_buf_cleanup(vdev);
 
+	vfio_pci_core_disable(vdev);
+
 	mutex_lock(&vdev->igate);
 	vfio_pci_eventfd_replace_locked(vdev, &vdev->err_trigger, NULL);
 	vfio_pci_eventfd_replace_locked(vdev, &vdev->req_trigger, NULL);
 	mutex_unlock(&vdev->igate);
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(vfio_pci_core_close_device);

Calling `vfio_pci_core_disable()` first clears the Memory Space Enable (MSE) and releases BAR resources. However, DMABUFs may still hold references and can access the BARs until `vfio_pci_dma_buf_cleanup()` is called, creating a window for use-after-free or access to reassigned resources.

Calling `vfio_pci_dma_buf_cleanup()` first revokes all DMABUF references and access to the BARs. Then `vfio_pci_core_disable()` safely disables the function without risk of concurrent access via stale DMABUFs.
